title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'surgery' of conformal surfaces (cote 67). The previous page sets up an equivalence of categories. Conformal surfaces possibly with boundary, possibly non-orientable, correspond to holomorphic surfaces without boundary equipped with an anti-holomorphic involution σ. The correspondence is X ↦ (X^or, σ), where X^or is the complex/orientation (Schottky–Klein) double, with inverse X = X^or/σ. X is called hyperbolic iff X^or is. For compact X this means χ(X) < 0, using χ(X^or) = 2χ(X).

This page:
(1) If X is hyperbolic, the Poincaré metric of curvature −1 on X^or is invariant under every conformal and anti-conformal automorphism, in particular σ. It therefore descends to a hyperbolic metric on X. The boundary ∂X is the image of the fixed locus of σ. The fixed locus of an isometric involution is totally geodesic, so ∂X is geodesic.
(2) More generally, suppose X^or carries a 'canonical' metric invariant under conformal automorphisms, or merely under anti-involutions. The latter also covers X^or ≅ C: anti-involutions z ↦ a z̄ + b have |a| = 1 and so preserve the flat metric. Then this metric descends to X, again with geodesic boundary. For X without boundary, the descended metric agrees with the canonical metric considered earlier. Such a canonical metric exists in all cases except X ≅ P^1_C, which has no metric invariant under all of PGL_2(C).
(3) Caveat 1, X = RP^2. Here X^or = P^1 with the antipodal involution, and the bare prescription gives no metric. It does give one if we require the metric to lie in the class R(X^or) of 'distinguished' (round, constant-curvature) metrics and to be σ-stable. That determines it uniquely. In modern terms, round metrics of fixed area form PGL_2(C)/PSU(2) = H^3. The antipodal map acts on H^3 as an isometric involution with a unique fixed point, so the metric is unique.
(4) Caveat 2, X ≅ C. Here X^or ≅ C ⊔ C with σ swapping the components. The direct procedure gives a metric only up to a constant; the page breaks off there.

The next page goes on to the genuinely new cases: X connected with ∂X ≠ ∅, whose double 𝔛 is C (closed half-plane), and so on. The aim is to attach a canonical metric to every conformal surface with boundary, presumably to do conformal surgery by gluing along geodesic boundaries.
errors: No substantive errors. The claim 'invariant by all conformal automorphisms except when X^or ≅ C' is only meaningful up to a constant scale for flat cases; the author clearly intends metrics normalized or mod constants, as he says later.
'Sauf X ≅ P^1_C' and the RP^2 caveat are consistent: P^1 lacks an Aut-invariant metric, but the antipodal σ picks out a unique round metric.

ideas.what: Equivalence between conformal surfaces with boundary (possibly non-orientable) and Riemann surfaces without boundary with anti-holomorphic involution
ideas.modern_name: Schottky/Klein double; symmetric Riemann surfaces (Klein surfaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Klein, F. Schottky (19th c.); Alling–Greenleaf (1971)

ideas.what: Hyperbolic metric of the double descends to a hyperbolic metric on X with geodesic boundary
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of bordered Riemann surfaces / hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary via doubling
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Koebe, Poincaré); standard in Teichmüller theory

ideas.what: Canonical metric on RP^2 as the unique antipodally invariant round metric on P^1
ideas.modern_name: Fixed point of an isometric involution of H^3 = space of round metrics

ideas.what: Program of assigning a canonical metric to every conformal surface (with boundary) for surgery purposes
ideas.modern_name: Canonical metrics for gluing/plumbing of Riemann surfaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to surgery and the Teichmüller tower but not this metric bookkeeping

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but classical bookkeeping: doubling, descending invariant metrics, geodesic boundary, and the RP^2 and C special cases. All standard. The interest is only biographical, as evidence of Grothendieck preparing a canonical-metric framework for 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes'.
transcription_corrections: The superscript written 'X^σ' throughout is more plausibly X^or (orientation/complex double), consistent with the previous page.

The bracket likely reads '[ou seulement par antiinvolutions, ce qui est le cas aussi si X^or ≃ C]' rather than '[ou même par antiautomorphismes, ce qui est le cas sauf si X^σ ≃ C]'. This reading is mathematically correct, since anti-involutions of C are isometries of the flat metric.
'X, au bord géodésique' should read 'sur X, à bord géodésique'.
Line order: 'la métrique obtenue sur X est celle déjà envisagée — il y en a dans tous les cas, sauf X ≃ P^1_C'.
'la deuxième prescription' may be 'la dernière prescription'.
